summary.text: Jeff Hurd is the Republican U.S. Representative for Colorado's 3rd Congressional District, first elected in 2024, and won re-election on November 3, 2026, according to unofficial results.

A Grand Junction native and attorney, he practiced law in New York and western Colorado before entering Congress and sits on the Natural Resources, Transportation and Infrastructure, and Science, Space, and Technology committees.
He won renomination in the June 30, 2026 Republican primary.

paragraphs.text: Hurd was born in Grand Junction, Colorado, in 1979, and according to his official biography he grew up there; his first job was bagging groceries at a local store.
He earned a bachelor's degree in liberal studies from the University of Notre Dame, a J.D. from the University of Denver Sturm College of Law in 2008, and an LL.M. from Columbia Law School in 2010.
He worked at the Grand Junction Area Chamber of Commerce and clerked for 10th Circuit Judge Timothy Tymkovich.

According to his official biography, Hurd practiced law at Sullivan & Cromwell in New York City before returning to western Colorado, where he built a law practice focused primarily on rural electric cooperatives; Ballotpedia lists him as co-owner of a law firm.
Hurd won the November 2024 general election with 50.8% of the vote over Democrat Adam Frisch (45.8%), succeeding Lauren Boebert, and took office on January 3, 2025.
His committee assignments for 2025-2026 are Natural Resources, where he chairs the Indian and Insular Affairs Subcommittee, Transportation and Infrastructure, and Science, Space, and Technology.
He defeated Ron Hanks in the June 30, 2026 Republican primary, 66.4% to 33.6%.
His official biography states that he lives in Grand Junction with his wife, Barbora, and their five children.
He won the November 3, 2026 general election with 49.3% of the vote to Dwayne Romero's 47.4%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
